message: Superseded date. DOJ's interim final rule (signed 2026-04-16, effective on publication 2026-04-20) moved the ADA Title II web deadline for public entities of 50,000 or more from April 24, 2026 to April 26, 2027 - 28 CFR 35.200(b).
Superseded date in ISO form. The ADA Title II deadline for public entities of 50,000 or more is now 2027-04-26, not 2026-04-24.
Superseded date. HHS extended the Section 504 web and mobile accessibility deadline on 2026-05-07: recipients with 15 or more employees now have until May 11, 2027.
Superseded date in ISO form. The HHS Section 504 deadline for recipients with 15 or more employees is now 2027-05-11, not 2026-05-11.
Superseded date. HHS recipients with fewer than 15 employees moved from May 10, 2027 to May 10, 2028 in the same 2026-05-07 extension.

Ambiguous since the 2026 extension. April 26, 2027 is now the ADA Title II deadline for public entities of 50,000 or more. It used to be the date for smaller entities and special districts, which is now April 26, 2028. Confirm which tier this line means.
ADA Title II (28 CFR 35.200) and HHS Section 504 (45 CFR 84.84) both adopt WCAG 2.1 Level AA. A conformance claim written against WCAG 2.0 does not meet either rule.
Level A is not enough. Both the ADA Title II rule and the HHS Section 504 rule require WCAG 2.1 Level AA.

Section 508 governs federal agencies. State and local government web content is governed by 28 CFR 35.200 and HHS-funded recipients by 45 CFR 84.84 - both point at WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Cite the rule that actually covers this entity.
WCAG 2.2 Level AA contains everything in 2.1 Level AA, so meeting it is fine. The conformance statement should still cite WCAG 2.1 Level AA, which is the standard the two rules adopt.
Unverifiable conformance claim. No agency certifies ADA compliance, and a blanket claim is the sentence a demand letter quotes back. State the standard, the date tested and the known gaps instead.
img element with no alt attribute - WCAG 2.1 SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A).
html element with no lang attribute - WCAG 2.1 SC 3.1.1 Language of Page (Level A).
input with no id, aria-label or aria-labelledby, so no label can be attached to it - WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A).
Link text that means nothing out of context - WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (Level A). Screen reader users pull links out into a list.
Positive tabindex overrides the document focus order - WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A). Use 0 or -1.
Click handler on a non-interactive element: no keyboard access and no role - WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A) and SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A).
role=button on an element that cannot take focus - WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A). Add tabindex=0 and a key handler, or use a real button element.
Focus outline removed - WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA). Replace it with a visible focus style rather than deleting it.
Zoom blocked in the viewport meta tag - WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.4 Resize Text (Level AA).
iframe with no title attribute - WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A).
Media set to autoplay - WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.2 Audio Control (Level A) once it runs longer than three seconds.
Content that moves or blinks with no way to stop it - WCAG 2.1 SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (Level A).
Focusable element hidden from assistive technology: it stays in the tab order with no accessible name - WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A).

Link to a conventional electronic document. Under 28 CFR 35.201 these are excepted only when they were posted before the entity's compliance date and are not currently used to apply for or take part in a service. Record which exception you rely on, or make the file conform.
Third-party embed. The third-party exception in 28 CFR 35.201 does not cover content a contractor posts on the public entity's behalf - check who owns this embed before relying on it.
